text: A Transform Map is the piece that finally moves data out of the raw staging table and into a real target table, like sys_user or a custom table with its own business logic. The Data Source decided how data got into staging. The Transform Map decides what happens to it from here on.

Field mapping is the heart of it: a list of pairs, each connecting one staging column to one target field. A source column called emp_email can map to a target field called email, or dept_code can map to department as a reference lookup. The names don't have to match between the two sides, because the map is exactly where that translation happens, field by field.

Running the same import twice with no safeguard in place would simply create a brand new duplicate record every single time. Coalesce is the fix for that. You mark one field, or a combination of fields, as the coalesce field, and the transform checks whether a matching record already exists before it does anything else.

If a match is found on that coalesce field, the existing record gets updated with the new row's values. If no match is found, a brand new record is inserted instead. That insert-or-update behavior is commonly called an upsert, and coalesce is ServiceNow's real, built-in mechanism for it.

For a sys_user import, email makes a natural coalesce field — it's unique per person and stays stable across every reimport. Get coalesce wrong, or skip setting it entirely, and a second run of the same import will quietly fill the target table with duplicate records nobody asked for.

Not every field is a simple straight copy. When a target field needs real logic — combining two staging columns together, or applying a conditional business rule — a Run Script transform handles it instead. Deep scripting technique for cases like that comes later in this path, in the Scripting and Application Development course.
Field mapping connects the columns. Coalesce prevents the duplicates. Next up: putting the entire pipeline together in a worked, end-to-end import and transform lab.
